title: Quantum Algorithms for Modular Factorials
summary: We give a bounded-error quantum algorithm that, given a prime $p$, a divisor $q\mid(p-1)$, and an integer $0<n<p$, computes $n!\bmod p$ in expected time $\widetilde{O}(q^c+\sqrt{p/q})$ for some absolute constant $c\ge 1$. When $p-1$ has a divisor of size $q\approx p^{1/(2c+1)}$, this gives the exponent $c/(2c+1)<1/2$. To our knowledge, this is the first algorithm to break the exponent $1/2$ barrier for modular factorials under such a divisor promise.
